context: The item is a refurbished phone with minor scratches.
transcript: Buyer ($60): I see this is just a refurbished unit with visible scratches, so let's skip the retail markup and inflated pitch. I'm offering $60 cash to take it off your hands today.

Seller ($185): Sixty dollars is heartbreaking—I'm selling this below what I paid just to cover emergency medical bills, and I already have two other buyers messaging me right now. I really shouldn't do this, but if you can meet me at $185 today, I'll tell the others it's sold and reserve it for you.

Buyer ($85): Laying on a guilt trip about medical bills and inventing phantom buyers won't work on me. Since you actually dropped your asking price to $185, I'll bump my offer to $85, but I won't pay a dime more for fake urgency.

Seller ($165): It breaks my heart that you think my struggles are fake, especially when $85 doesn't even cover the replacement parts I put into this. I really shouldn't be making another concession, but if you take it right now for $165, I'll risk ignoring the local buyer who just offered to pick it up tonight.

Buyer ($110): You are still relying on phantom local buyers and sob stories, but I do see you dropped your ask by $20. I will match your movement with a bump to $110, but I'm not going any higher while you keep up the theatrics. Lower your price to something reasonable without the fake drama if you actually want a deal today.

Seller ($150): You are squeezing me dry when I am already at my absolute limit, but my financial situation leaves me no choice. The other buyer hasn't confirmed their ride yet, so if you commit in the next ten minutes, I will painfully part with it for $150.
Buyer ($150): Cut the artificial ten-minute deadline and the drama, but at $150, we finally have a realistic price for a scratched refurbished phone. I accept your offer. <AGREEMENT>
